clue.text: New cheese, provided much

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'New cheese, provided much (2,5)': N + BRIE inside IF gives the letters, but no word defines the answer and no word signals the container; the clue looks garbled by OCR and no search found the original.

clue.text: Wrong taking it round the Channel Islands? Certainly not right

parts.note: wrong in the sense of ailing or bad, as in feeling ill

indicators.note: round says the word it is wrapped about the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
CI is the standard abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Someone smuggling something around the Channel Islands is told it is definitely not proper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British crown dependencies off Normandy (Jersey, Guernsey and others), abbreviated CI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful or forbidden is plainly not right or permitted.

clue.text: Dull person following recipe instruction to make sweet

indicators.note: following places the dull person's word after the recipe instruction

parts.note: a recipe might tell the cook to bake well
a pudding is British slang for a slow, stolid person

explanation.surface: A cook mutters that a dim companion has been trailing the recipe to produce a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bakewell pudding is a jam-and-almond dessert from the Derbyshire town of Bakewell; 'sweet' is the British word for a dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond and jam tart-like dessert is served as a pudding course, which British speakers call a sweet.

clue.text: Pause in terrible duel after artist's dispatched father

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled duel at the end, behind the trimmed artist
dispatched means sent away, so the father's letters leave the artist's word

parts.note: a painter is an artist
PA is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: terrible signals that the word duel is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful fight halts once the painter has killed off his own parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched' looks like a word for killing in a duel, but here it just means sent away, and 'terrible' is the anagram signal for the duel.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval or break between acts of a play is a short pause in proceedings.

clue.text: Father's always less restrained

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A priest's habit is to be more relaxed than others.
explanation.definitionFit: Being freer means having fewer limits or constraints, so less held back.

clue.text: French boat containing nothing ornate

indicators.note: containing says the boat holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: barque is a sailing vessel, the word coming via French
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A vessel from France carries no cargo but is richly decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: The style of seventeenth-century art and architecture is noted for heavy, elaborate decoration.

clue.text: Commanded ruler to imprison every singer

indicators.note: to imprison means to lock something inside, so the last piece goes within the first

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, meaning commanded
all can mean every one
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch was ordered to lock up every vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a performer of ballads, songs that tell a story.

clue.text: Tear and hesitation showing more maturity

parts.note: to rip is to tear
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Ripping and dithering are presented as signs of growing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or people that are further developed are more mature, fully ready.

clue.text: Article seen in bridge player's card -a club?

indicators.note: seen in places the article within the card's name

parts.note: at bridge the players are North, South, East and West, so a card held by South could be his queen
the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone at the bridge table spots a word on one of their cards that turns out to be a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen of the South is a Scottish football club from Dumfries; 'club' also teases the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen of the South is a professional Scottish football side, so a club in the sporting sense.

clue.text: Festival, new, of oriental origin

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: A fresh springtime festival is said to have come from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things coming from the East.

clue.text: Quickly copying an audience?

definitions.meaning: a British idiom for very fast, as in running flat out
an audience claps, so doing the same as those applauding

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at great speed, and read literally it means imitating people who applaud.

clue.text: Poet with no little power to make you cringe

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is dropped from the poet's name

parts.note: William Cowper was an eighteenth-century English poet
P is the abbreviation for power, little meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: A poet who is barely powerful makes readers shrink back.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back in fear is to cringe or cower.

clue.text: Plan again to bring up a variety of topics?

parts.note: to rear children is to bring them up
a range is a spread or variety, as in a range of subjects

explanation.surface: A speaker reorganises so as to raise a wide spread of subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorganise something is to set it out in a different order, planning it afresh.

clue.text: -record leader of union taking stroll round

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '-record leader of union taking stroll round (9)': LP + U inside TODDLE gives the letters, but the opening of the clue, which should define the Dorset village, is lost and no search found it.

clue.text: Sweet's found under bowl almost entirely upset

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts the sweet below the trimmed bowl
almost entirely says the word is used all but its final letter

parts.note: a dish is a bowl
a comfit is a sugared sweet

explanation.surface: A sweet is discovered beneath a bowl, nearly everything having been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' takes the last letter H off DISH, leaving DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To discomfit someone is to unsettle or embarrass them.

clue.text: into ebbing river

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'into ebbing river (5)': the start is cut off; F inside a reversed NILE gives the letters, but the definition and the word supplying F are missing and no search found them.

clue.text: Very erotic, topless, embracing top half of tremendous lover, initially

indicators.note: embracing means holding the following pieces inside the outer word
topless means the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: sexy means erotic

indicators.note: top half of takes the first five of the ten letters
initially takes just the first letter of lover

explanation.surface: A racy tabloid scene in which a topless figure clutches a wonderful lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface hides plain mechanics: 'topless' beheads one word and 'top half of' halves another, so both 'top' words do different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, both words mean to a great degree.

clue.text: Father's swallowed up by last of horrible insect forms

indicators.note: swallowed says one piece goes down inside the other

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father; the 's reads as has
taken as written

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of horrible

explanation.surface: Dad has gulped down something nasty at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupae are the dormant stage between larva and adult, so forms an insect takes.

clue.text: Suggests taking part in concerts

indicators.note: taking means the concerts hold the next piece within them

parts.note: the Proms are the BBC's summer series of promenade concerts in London

explanation.surface: Someone proposes joining in a series of concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous annual season of classical concerts at London's Royal Albert Hall.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to nudge or suggest what they should say or do.

clue.text: An extension of emergency health operations?

definitions.text: An extension of emergency health operations?

parts.words: An extension of emergency health operations?
parts.note: reads as a report about lengthening hospital surgery, but means something that stretches, the frame carrying casualties in an emergency

explanation.definitionFit: The canvas frame for carrying the injured is a tool of emergency care, and the word also means something that extends.

clue.text: Jogs on motorway in Germany heading for Stuttgart

parts.note: re means on or concerning
M is the British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of Stuttgart

explanation.surface: Someone runs along the autobahn in Germany making for Stuttgart.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog the memory is to prompt it, which is what a reminder does.

clue.text: Rum and a beer -no way to be an exceptional character

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a means one

indicators.note: no says the way's letters are left out of the beer

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A drinker orders rum and a beer, then finds there is no route home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no way' removes ST from STOUT, leaving OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who differs from all the rest of a group is a misfit or exception.

clue.text: Fool with soldiers' source of explosive

parts.note: a nit is a silly person
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An idiot hangs about with army men near something that blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a key ingredient of gunpowder.

clue.text: Implements left to be coated with carbon, all over

indicators.note: all over means turned right round, so the whole piece is read backwards
to be coated with puts the letter for left inside the carbon word

parts.note: soot is carbon deposited by burning

explanation.surface: Equipment left lying around ends up covered all over in carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside SOOT to make SLOOT, and 'all over' turns that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Implements and tools are both instruments used for work.

clue.text: Racecourse traduced in poems

indicators.note: traduced means misrepresented, so the letters of poems are twisted

explanation.surface: A racetrack is slandered in some verses.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs, in Surrey, is the English racecourse that hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is the racecourse home of the Derby.

clue.text: Significance of poor investment? but one's committed now!

parts.note: the point of something is its significance
taken as written
a bad investment yields no return

explanation.surface: An investor regrets a bad deal but realises it is too late to back out.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage beyond which turning back is impossible is where a person is fully committed.

clue.text: Good fellows in group? Just a bit

indicators.note: in places the good fellows within the group

parts.note: a set is a group
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Decent chaps within a club form only a small part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a piece or portion of a whole.

clue.text: Cuts made by openers for Yorkshire team in Sunday game, mostly

indicators.note: in places the openers within the Sunday game
mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: openers for takes the first letters, a cricket pun on opening batsmen

explanation.surface: Yorkshire's opening batsmen take part in a Sunday match and mostly score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final S of CHESS, leaving CHES; Y and T go inside S + CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To scythe grass is to mow or cut it with a long curved blade.
